newsitem.title: USA: Dry weather seen threat to Minnesota crops.
newsitem.headline: Dry weather seen threat to Minnesota crops.

text.p: Exceptionally dry weather across Minnesota during the last week led to increased concern about drought, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
"The week was seasonally warm but exceptionally dry across the state, and concern about potential drought has been spreading quickly," the report said.
Despite some isolated thunderstorms, it said, "rain gauges at many southern Minnesota points showed light, or zero precipitation" for the week.
Topsoil moisture was rated 29 percent very short, 41 percent short and 30 percent adequate.
Soybeans had emerged on an estimated 93 percent of the state's acreage, up from a five-year average of 79 percent.
"Later plantings show some uneven emergence from the dryness," the report said.
Spring wheat was 98 percent emerged, up from an average of 96 percent. It was 22 percent jointed, down from a normal 46 percent.
Corn was 99 percent emerged versus a five-year average of 95 percent.
